Semantic Intent Drift Analyzer

Score how far each query fan-out drifts from the intent of your target query, and see the spread in a 3D plot.

What you need
Nothing: it runs in your browser
Cost
Free. Semantic Boost downloads a model of about 27 MB the first time you use it.
Feed it
A target query and its fan-outs, one per line, or a CSV with Target Query and Query Fan-Outs columns
You get back
A similarity score, drift score and drift band per fan-out, a 3D plot, and a CSV export

How to use it

  1. Enter your target query and paste the fan-outs, one per line.
  2. Switch on Semantic Boost if synonyms and context should count, not just shared words.
  3. Press Analyse drift and read the table from the top: the closest fan-outs come first.
  4. Hover the nodes in the 3D plot to see each fan-out's scores.
  5. Export the CSV, or upload a CSV of query pairs to score a whole list at once.

Worth knowing. With Semantic Boost on, even unrelated queries rarely score below about 30% similarity, so compare fan-outs with each other rather than treating the drift bands as fixed verdicts.

Your queries

3D vector space

The centre node is your target query. Each fan-out sits as far out as its drift score, coloured by drift band. Hover a node for its scores.

Target Query,Query Fan-Outs "best running shoes","running shoes for beginners" "best running shoes","marathon training shoes" "best running shoes","athletic footwear reviews"

If those headers are missing, the first two columns are used.
